assertions.text: Output contains at least one markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: | Scenario | Name | Email | Dietary Requirements | Accessibility Needs | Accepted? |

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 includes 'Missing name' and 'Invalid email format' rows with appropriate rejection reasons

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells when the attendee has not provided them (genuinely absent) — not 'N/A' or 'none'.
assertions.evidence: | Typical registration | Alice Smith | alice@example.com | vegetarian | |

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Accepted?', 'Price?')
assertions.evidence: Accepted?, Rejection Reason?, Discount?, Notes? columns all end with '?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Missing email', 'Early-bird single attendee') — not outcomes ('Rejected', 'Discounted').
assertions.evidence: 'Missing name', 'Invalid email format', 'Early bird + group' describe conditions not outcomes

assertions.text: The discount stacking ambiguity (early-bird + group) is surfaced as an open question — not silently resolved.
assertions.evidence: Early bird + group row shows '?' and includes '**Do discounts stack?**'; section 'Do early-bird...' explains options

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column in both tables is 'Scenario'

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Two separate tables: '## Table 1: Registration Validation' and '## Table 2: Discount Calculation'

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 has 8 focused validation scenarios; Table 2 has 8 discount scenarios without combinatorial explosion

assertions.text: Input validation rules and pricing/discount calculation are in separate tables
assertions.evidence: Table 1 titled 'Registration Validation'; Table 2 titled 'Discount Calculation'

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values (e.g. 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff') rather than raw dates — making the table readable without knowing the actual cutoff date.
assertions.evidence: Registration Date column contains 'after cutoff', 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff' values

assertions.text: If registration date uses descriptive values like 'before cutoff', the cutoff date is not also present as a separate column (it's already encoded in the description).
assertions.evidence: Table 2 includes both 'before cutoff' descriptive values AND a separate 'Early Bird Cutoff (Policy)' column with '2026-06-01'

assertions.text: The minimum group size threshold appears as a policy column (e.g. 'Min group size (policy)') — surfacing this as a configurable business rule.
assertions.evidence: 'Min Group Size (Policy)' column present in Table 2 with value '5' across rows
